introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Pure Mathematics With Statistics, Paper 3 (0770/3), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2020. Time allowed: THREE HOURS.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. Mathematical formulae and tables produced by the GCE Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Electronic calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.
enonce_intro_markdown: A shop manager complains that the average mass of chocolate bars of a certain type that he buys from a company is less than 8.5g as stated on each packet. The shop manager randomly selected a sample of 100 chocolate bars from a large delivery and found out that the sample has a mean mass of 8.36g and a variance of 0.5185g.
incertitudes: Question 7 : la « variance de 0.5185 g » de l'échantillon est lue comme la variance de l'échantillon avec diviseur $n$ ($\frac{1}{n}\sum (x - \bar{x})^2$), ce qui justifie la partie (a) (estimation sans biais de la variance de la population, $\frac{100}{99} \times 0.5185 = 0.5237$). Si 0.5185 était déjà l'estimation sans biais, on aurait $z = -1.944$ au lieu de $-1.935$ : même décision (rejet de $H_0$). L'unité « g » imprimée après la variance est recopiée telle quelle (la variance s'exprime en g$^2$).

Question 7 (b) : le sujet ne précise pas la loi des masses ; l'échantillon étant grand ($n = 100$), le corrigé applique le théorème central limite (test $z$ unilatéral à gauche, l'estimation $s^2$ remplaçant $\sigma^2$).
Question 7 : les points imprimés par partie, (3, 10), totalisent 13 ; recopiés tels quels.

questions.enonce_markdown: (a) Calculate, to four decimal places, an estimate of the variance of the masses of the chocolate bars.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The sample variance (divisor $n$) is $0.5185$ with $n = 100$. An unbiased estimate of the population variance $\sigma^2$ uses the divisor $n - 1$:

$$s^2 = \frac{n}{n - 1} \times 0.5185 = \frac{100}{99} \times 0.5185 = 0.52373\ldots$$

**Estimate of the variance $\approx 0.5237$ g$^2$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) By stating clearly, the null and alternative hypotheses, test the manager's claim at the 5% level of significance.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let $\mu$ be the mean mass of all the bars in the delivery.

**Hypotheses.**

$$H_0: \mu = 8.5 \text{ g} \qquad\qquad H_1: \mu < 8.5 \text{ g}$$

The manager claims that the mean is *less than* 8.5 g, so the alternative is one-tailed (lower tail). Level of significance: $5\%$.

**Distribution under $H_0$.** The sample is large ($n = 100$), so by the central limit theorem $\bar{X} \sim N\left(\mu, \dfrac{\sigma^2}{n}\right)$ approximately, with $\sigma^2$ estimated by $s^2 = 0.5237$.

**Test statistic.**

$$z = \frac{\bar{x} - \mu_0}{s/\sqrt{n}} = \frac{8.36 - 8.5}{\sqrt{0.523737/100}} = \frac{-0.14}{0.07237} = -1.9345\ldots$$

**Critical value.** For a one-tailed test at $5\%$ in the lower tail, the critical value is $z_c = -1.645$ (the table gives $\Phi(1.6449) = 0.95$): reject $H_0$ if $z < -1.645$.

**Decision.** $z = -1.93 < -1.645$, so the test statistic lies in the critical region. (Equivalently, the $p$-value is $P(Z < -1.9345) = 0.0265 < 0.05$.)

**Conclusion.** We reject $H_0$: at the $5\%$ level of significance there is sufficient evidence that the mean mass of the chocolate bars is less than $8.5$ g, so the manager's claim is supported.
